雄心勃勃并成为一名父亲

Being ambitious and being a dad

科技产品 作者 nichochar 热度 699 回复 515 2026/08/17 00:08
打开原帖 打开外部链接 JSON

摘要

  • Being ambitious and being a dad When I was going through YC, I didn’t mention my seven month old daughter to anyone. Now a few years later I have two kids, a dog and a very packed schedule. My kids are the best thing in my life. For years, my work was my life. Now my life competes with my work. I don’t think I’m alone. Here’s Paul Graham in Having Kids:
  • Some of my worries about having kids were right, though. They definitely make you less productive. I know having kids makes some people get their act together, but if your act was already together, you’re going to have less time to do it in.

年龄越大，我越意识到雄心勃勃，而“雄心勃勃”是一种完全错误的人生方向。

他人认可的机会并不是做出这样或那样的选择的好理由，由这种选择组成的生活最终会让你在精神上破产。

根据你所热衷的事情、基于什么会给你的生活带来并保持有意义的关系、基于什么会让你养成习惯来做出决定。你在户外，沐浴在阳光下，活动身体，健康饮食，当然，这会让你有能力支付这些费用。

关注过程，而不是结果。

根据什么能让你更“成功”做出决定，会让你成为别人认可的奴隶。而那些人会耗尽你的精力，浪费你的生命来实现他们自己的目标。

此外，如果你选择了正确的伴侣，生孩子会同时带来生活中所有美好的事情。这是让自己进入美好生活的最有效方式。

The older I get the more I realize ambition and "being ambitious" is a completely misplaced way to orient your life.

The chance of validation from others is not a good reason for making one choice or another and a life made of choices of that kind will eventually leave you spiritually bankrupt.

Make decisions based on what you're passionate about, based on what will bring and keep meaningful relationships into your life, based on what will leave you with habits that take you outside, into the sun, moving your body and eating healthy, and, sure, that will afford you the ability to pay for those things.

Focus on the process, not the outcome.

Making decisions based on what will make you more "successful" will make you a slave to others approval. And those others will use you up and waste your life to achieve their own objectives.

Also, if you pick the right partner, having kids does all the good things in life at once. It is the most efficient way to get yourself into the good life possible.

雄心勃勃并不一定意味着您的目标是获得验证。这意味着您正在瞄准一个具有挑战性的目标。驱动这一雄心壮志的因素才是最重要的。

许多人的驱动力是创造真正的改变、建设、解决问题和/或帮助人们的愿望。许多人这样做只是因为它很有趣，但这并没有降低他们的雄心。

Being ambitious doesn't necessarily mean you're aiming for validation. It means you're aiming for a goal that's challenging. What drives that ambition is what matters.

Many are driven by a desire to create real change, a desire to build, to solve a problem, and/or help people. Many do it simply because it's fun, but it doesn't make them any less ambitious.

我参加了 2016 年夏季批次。十年后的时光似乎足够长，足以让我们反思美好的生活。我这批人中有些人雄心勃勃，不是为了攀登别人的公司阶梯，而是为了建立自己的庞大/成功/富裕的公司。

对于那些将其与他们所热衷的事情分开的人来说，这里我指的是影响，而不是“热衷于建立一个大企业，已经发生过多次崩溃。存在危机，极端在线综合症，把他们带入了一个风投们所说的或与 Tech Crunch 上的新闻稿竞争的世界。定义他们的自我价值。

这些人通常不快乐！但很多人并不快乐。

那些以技术或公司建设作为实现更大目标的创始人，他们可能会或可能不会继续在其他有影响力的公司或组织工作。他们似乎对生活和对公司的贡献更加满意。

这种野心是健康的、有意义的、持久的。这并不是说这些人没有野心——他们非常有野心！但这不是“大公司的好事”，而是“有巨大的积极影响的好事”。

I can +1 who you're replying to in the context of founders and achieving a large dream (building a massive company.)

I was in the Summer 2016 batch. Ten years out feels like long enough for some reflections on lives well-lived. There were people in my batch who were ambitious, not in climbing someone else's corporate ladder but in building their own massive/successful/wealthy company.

For those who separated it from what they were passionate about—and here I mean the impact, not "passionate about building a big business—there have been more than a few crash outs. Existential crises, Extremely Online Syndrome, pulled into a world where what VCs say or competition with press releases on Tech Crunch define their self-worth.

These people are generally not happy. Some are! But many are not.

The founders who worked on things that they care about, with technology or company-building as a _means_ to achieving some greater end, are doing much better. They might or might not still be at their start-ups. Many have gone on to work at other impactful companies or organizations. They seem much more content with life and their contributions to the world.

That's the type of ambition that is healthy _and_ meaningful _and_ lasting. It's not that these people aren't ambitious—they very much are! But it's not "big company good". It's "big positive impact good."

Aurornis 2026/08/19 23:35
回想起来，我发现大多数互联网评论部分关于生孩子的建议都是无益的。有一句陈词滥调可以用 1000 种不同的方式来表达：“工作量很大，我的孩子让我发疯，但我不会用它来换取整个世界”。现在我是一名家长，这些建议感觉过分夸大了负面因素，并且无法解释为什么人们喜欢他们的孩子。

说实话，很难与非父母理解为什么你喜欢自己的孩子。这与照顾别人的孩子完全不同。这是你的家人，你喜欢和他们在一起。下班后，我宁愿和孩子们一起出去骑自行车或和他们一起拼搭乐高积木，而不是放松地看电视。我有点害怕有一天他们不想花那么多时间和我在一起，因为我们玩得很开心。早点完成工作并早点开始新的一天是一种额外的动力，这样我就可以有更多的时间和他们在一起，这是我作为一个夜以继日的人从来没有想过会说的话。

额外的工作比我没有孩子、下班后和周末放松要多，但这并不像一些人谈论的那样是世界末日的苦差事。他们在夜间醒来并需要不断的喂养和变化的早期阶段很快就过去了，然后你就进入了日常生活并教他们更加自给自足。我不会详述它，或者至少不会让它成为你想象与家人共度余生的障碍。拥有一个家庭 40 年，需要一两年改变睡眠时间表。

从周围快乐的父母那里获得平衡的看法是个好主意。在网上，很容易陷入社交媒体的漩涡，因为父母会发泄不满，但我发现最好的建议来自于你周围快乐的父母，他们安静地享受自己的生活，而不会提起孩子的话题。你必须和他们一起提出来。根据您工作的地点，您周围的普通人可能有一个家庭并且对此感到高兴，但他们不会一直提起这件事，因为这对他们来说只是正常的生活。

Looking back, I found most Internet comment section advice about having kids to be unhelpful. There’s a cliche that gets rephrased 1000 different ways to say a variation of “It’s a lot of work and my kids drive me crazy but I wouldn’t trade it for the world”. Now that I am a parent that advice feels like it oversells the negatives and fails to explain why people like their kids.

Truthfully, it is hard to relate to non-parents why you enjoy your own kids. It’s completely different than babysitting someone else’s kids. It’s your family and you like being with them. After work I’d rather hang out with my kids and go for a bike ride or build legos with them instead of relax and watch TV. I’m kind of dreading the day that they don’t want to spend so much time with me because we have so much fun. It’s a little extra motivation to get my work done early and start my day early so I can have more time with them, which is something I never thought I’d say as a nights and evenings person.

The extra work is more work than if I didn’t have kids and just relaxed after work and on weekends, but it’s not the world-ending grind like some people talk about. The early part where they’re waking up through the night and need constant feedings and changes goes by quickly and then you’re into a routine and teaching them ever more self sufficiency. I wouldn’t dwell on it, or at least don’t let it be an obstacle to imagining the rest of your years with a family. It’s a year or two of altered sleep schedules for 40 years of having a family.

Getting balanced takes from happy parents around you is a good idea. Online it’s too easy to get drawn into social media whirlpools of unhappy parents venting about things, but I’ve found the best advice comes from the happy parents around you that are quietly enjoying their lives without bringing up the topic of kids. You have to bring it up with them. Depending on where you work, it’s possible that the average person around you has a family and is happy about it, but they’re not bringing it up all the time because it’s just normal life for them.
